blocks.text: The prefix design visits n values once to build and performs constant work for each of q queries, yielding O(n + q) total time. Under the stated worst case, each queried range has Θ(n) elements, so rescanning all q ranges takes Θ(n) × q = Θ(nq), represented by the offered O(nq). The separate prefix retains n + 1 boundary states, so its extra space is O(n).

Prefix time O(nq) discards the constant-time query benefit, O(q log n) omits the linear build and adds an unused search, and O(n²) cannot describe independent q. Rescan O(n + q) or O(q log n) understates Θ(n) work per worst-case query, while O(n² + q) wrongly replaces independent q with n. Prefix space is not O(1) or O(log n) because every boundary is stored, and not O(nq) because all queries reuse the same one-dimensional array.
